author: Amy Goodman
title: White House Says Venezuela Oil Grab Includes 100-Year Leases to 17 Oil Fields
content:
Economist Francisco Rodríguez says no Venezuelan government would enter such a deal unless they were “held at gunpoint.”

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The U.S. has struck a deal to take majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves, nine months after the U.S. military abducted President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores in a raid on Caracas and two months after The New York Times revealed that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has become the de facto viceroy of Venezuela, effectively controlling Venezuela’s finances, the distribution of its natural resources and its government. The new oil deal gives the Department of Defense a 35% stake in a joint U.S.-Venezuelan private company that now holds 100-year leases to 17 oil fields. It also gives the U.S. the right to buy some of the oil produced at cost — a major triumph for the Trump administration as the war on Iran depletes the United States’ strategic oil reserves. Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez claims U.S. investment in Venezuela’s oil industry will jumpstart the country’s floundering economy, but critics, including Venezuelan economist Francisco Rodríguez, say the deal is not only “unfavorable to Venezuela” but also appears to violate the Venezuelan Constitution.

“The whole history around this is extremely shady,” adds Rodríguez, who previously led Venezuela’s Congressional Budget Office and now teaches at the University of Denver. “It’s clear that this is not a deal that any Venezuelan government would have entered into unless this country had been subject to an invasion, and unless its authorities had been held at gunpoint. So, I think we’ve replaced gunboat diplomacy now for gunpoint diplomacy.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Nine months after the U.S. military abducted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and the first lady in a raid on Caracas, President Trump has announced a deal for the U.S. to take majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s proven oil reserves. In addition, the Pentagon will take partial ownership of a private firm at the center of the deal: North American Blue Energy Partners. Trump praised the deal Monday.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: We have a great relationship with Venezuela. It’s — you know, it’s a — it’s a team, in a sense, and we’re taking out millions and millions of barrels of oil, going to Houston, going to Louisiana, going to lots of different places in the United States and all over the world. And we’re doing — we’re making a fortune, and they’re making a fortune. They’re starting to make real money. And we have Exxon going in. We have Chevron going in. We have our big oil companies going in. And everybody’s bidding. …

So, you know, we do a lot of things. Here’s a deal that nobody’s ever heard of a deal like that. It may be the greatest deal ever made. Who knows? But it’s millions and million. Already we’ve paid for the war. The cost of the war has been paid for many, many times before. Where have you heard that before? You didn’t hear that with Afghanistan. You didn’t hear that with Vietnam and by people that ran it a lot differently than I run it.

AMY GOODMAN: On Saturday, Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodríguez defended the oil deal, insisting it’s beneficial for Venezuela.

PRESIDENT DELCY RODRÍGUEZ: [translated] In return, Venezuela receives production, employment, investment in infrastructure, higher revenues for the state and productive linkages for the national industry. The benefits are countless. This binational project, signed for 25 years, envisions the development of 17 strategic fields with a production target of more than 1.5 million barrels per day. This is solely under the binational agreement between Venezuela and the United States.

AMY GOODMAN: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen criticized the deal, saying, quote, “This is proof Trump put our service members at risk to get Venezuelan oil for his billionaire buddies. Putting our soldiers’ lives on the line for private profit is a gross dereliction of his constitutional duty,” Senator Van Hollen said.

The new oil deal comes two months after The New York Times revealed U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has become the de facto viceroy of Venezuela, effectively controlling Venezuela’s finances, the distribution of its natural resources and its government …

author: Daron Letts
title: Paddling on the curriculum at Victor Sammurtok School
content:
Textbooks and smart boards have nothing to do with the back-to-school experience for 26 high school students in Chesterfield Inlet.


Memphis Kreelak prepares to go underwater on Police Lake Aug. 20 in Chesterfield Inlet as teacher Glen Brocklebank assists with a controlled capsize. Keagan Kadjuk looks on. (Photo by Daron Letts)


They are participating in Victor Sammurtok School’s annual two-week Qajaq Program, in which they learn to paddle student-made qajait in freshwater and, ultimately, the open ocean.


“I wish it could last two months,” said senior student Vicky Kowtak as she pulled her craft to shore on Police Lake after capsizing — on purpose — on Aug. 20.


That was the second day of the program, when science teacher Glen Brocklebank helped the teens get comfortable tipping their qajait in shallow water, close to shore.


The students practised exiting their qajaq underwater, righting it, then re-entering until they could do so in under one minute. Once they mastered that skill, they had free rein to paddle at will in the centre of the lake.


The lake — 150-metres wide and 1.5 metres deep — is more of a pond, located at the end of the airport runway.


“There is no swimming pool in Chesterfield Inlet, so there’s some students that are very afraid of water,” Brocklebank said.


The students are equipped with life jackets and dry suits with a fleece under layer, paid for by a $140,000 Arctic Inspiration Prize in 2018.


Brocklebank and his spouse, English teacher Anna Leishman, supervise the students alongside nine experienced graduates who served as paid instructors.


“It’s a fun program and I love to help the students,” said one instructor, Hector Mullins, whose beaming smile never left his face throughout the morning of Aug. 20.


Elementary classes and some family members even watched from shore.


“It gives the students confidence,” said Susan Makpah, as she quietly cheered on her grandson, Cyrus Makpah.


The students needed that buoyed confidence on the fifth day, as they moved on to Mission Lake near the Co-op, which is twice as long and deep.


Winds gusted to 30 km/h, which added another challenge.


“They’re really keen kids,” said Leishman. “They listened and they really paid attention.”


On Day 6 they hit the ocean, hugging the shore at first as they paddled across the strait between the school and the docks, surrounded on three sides by land.


The next day was even more ambitious as the crew bussed one kilometre past the power plant and paddled back on the ocean.


“Every day is building in terms of difficulty,” Brocklebank said.


Brocklebank sometimes could only see the students’ helmets above the waves as their qajait pulsed up and down atop two-foot swells on Hudson Bay.


On Wednesday, the students will become teachers when they return to Police Lake and invite a friend or family member to try out their qajait.


In the fall, the school plans to purchase new gear with a $50,000 grant from the Isaksimagit Inuusirmi Katujjiqatigiit Embrace Life Council.

author: Unknown
title: Teachers and students: We reject restrictions on the Kurdish language
content:
Teachers and students in the cities of Kobanê and Hesekê held protests against the decision taken by the Education Ministry of the Syrian interim government.


Hesekê


Students held a protest outside the Hesekê Council building. A joint statement, prepared in Kurdish and Arabic, was read by Mihemed Hesen and Jiyan Meo.


The statement said: “Throughout our lives and during these past 14 years, we have known no schools other than those that opened the doors of science to us in our mother tongue.


This sudden decision is pushing us into extremely difficult circumstances for which we bear no responsibility.


Therefore, as the students of today and tomorrow, we call on the Syrian Ministry of Education to immediately reverse this decision and listen to the voices of us children and young people. We ask to be allowed to continue our education in our own language, in all scientific and literary subjects, in a way that guarantees our psychological and academic well-being and success.”


Kobanê


In Kobanê, teachers and students at Kobanê University also issued a press statement. The statement was read in Arabic and Kurdish by university academics Aras Hiso and Jiyan Osman.


The statement said: “Universities and linguistic communities view this step not simply as a reduction in the number of classes, but as a change to the role and mission of the Kurdish language within education. This is because, over the years, an educational model has been developed in which Kurdish is used as the primary language of instruction, and significant steps have been taken in developing the curriculum, educational materials, teaching staff, and scientific terminology.


Over the past more than 10 years, the use of Kurdish has not been limited to teaching language, literature, and social sciences; it has also extended to the natural sciences, mathematics, applied subjects, and different fields of knowledge. This experience has contributed to the development of Kurdish not merely as the subject of a single course, but as a language of education, knowledge, and scientific research.”


The statement added: “Based on this, Kobanê University calls on the relevant authorities to reconsider the decision to reduce Kurdish-language classes and to conduct comprehensive academic, educational, and sociolinguistic research before changing the existing educational system. It also calls for universities, researchers, and experts in language, education, and curriculum development to be included in any new vision concerning the future of the language of instruction.


Kobanê University believes that improving education is possible not by rolling back the rights that have been gained, but by building upon and further developing those existing achievements. Alongside strengthening the learning of other languages, protecting education in the mother tongue is the foundation of a multilingual, balanced, and sustainable education system.”

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Conservative Democrats Offer Amendment to Outdo GOP’s Condemnation of DSA
content:
The Democrats complained that Republicans weren’t taking the condemnation of socialism seriously enough.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A group of conservative Democrats in the House tried to one-up Republicans this week with a competing piece of legislation aimed at condemning the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and socialism in “all its forms,” after the GOP proposed an anti-socialist resolution that called for the passage of their marquee voter suppression legislation.

Last week, Republican Rep. Jeff Crank (Colorado) introduced a resolution that calls for the “condemnation and denouncement of socialism.” It calls out DSA, condemning the recent wave of DSA members running for Congress and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and says that DSA’s ideology is “incompatible with American values.”

The resolution clunkily segues into a call for the House to pass the GOP’s SAVE America Act, which puts burdensome restrictions on voting regarding ID requirements and proof of citizenship that civil rights advocates say would be the worst voter suppression bill ever passed by Congress.

The resolution reportedly infuriated some Democrats in the House — not because of the sweeping condemnation of an increasingly popular ideology among Democrats, but because the resolution contained the clause about passing SAVE America.

“This isn’t a serious bill,” said Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-New Jersey), per Axios. “If you actually want to take on socialism instead of playing political games, you don’t slip in the SAVE [America] Act as a poison pill that you know no Democrat will vote for.”

“To put the SAVE Act in there, it actually dilutes the power of what this socialism resolution is and and should be attempting to do,” Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-Michigan) told The Hill. “So you know our amendment just simply attempts to expose this fraudulent, insincere attempt by Republicans and say, ‘hey, if you guys really want to have a vote on socialism, let’s have it, right?’ And separate out these two issues.”

The resolution would do little to “take on” socialism, as it’s mostly symbolic. However, it comes as the Trump administration is conducting a fascist crackdown on Americans with left-wing beliefs, and as Democratic leaders like House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) are cozying up to the right in order to bash the left.

In response, Gottheimer and other conservative Democrats — Representatives Jared Moskowitz (Florida), Hillary Scholten (Michigan), and Tom Suozzi (New York) — offered their own amendment to the legislation that condemns socialism without the language about SAVE America. The amendment is slightly different from the Republican resolution, still condemning socialism and the DSA.

Republicans in the House Rules Committee advanced the resolution without the Democrats’ amendment.

Other conservative Democrats in the House signalled support for the resolution once it comes to a vote on the House floor, which could happen as soon as Tuesday. Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) said that he will “probably vote for” the resolution despite its inclusion of the pro-SAVE America language. Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas), the only Democrat to vote for the Save American Act when the House passed a version of the bill in February, declined to say how he plans to vote, according to Axios.

title: Iraqi and UN officials meet to discuss the situation in Shengal and return of IDPs
content:
According to Iraqi media, a comprehensive security and administrative meeting was held today under the chairmanship of General Abdul Amir al-Shammari, Deputy Chief of Staff and Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief.


The meeting was held in accordance with a decision by the Iraqi Prime Minister, and with the aim of ensuring stability, launching the reconstruction process and facilitating the return of displaced people to Shengal.


The meeting was reportedly attended by the National Security Adviser, the head of the National Security Service, the head of the National Intelligence Service, the Director of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office, and a number of security commanders.


The meeting highlighted the importance of eliminating the causes of displacement, providing essential services, restoring normal life to the region and developing appropriate solutions.


The Security Media Cell reported that the meeting focused on organizing and deploying security forces to enable the Shengal local administration to exercise its administrative authority normally, strengthening military coordination, activating the role of the local police and ending the presence of armed groups.


Abdul Amir al-Shammari reportedly drew attention to the issue of displaced people during the meeting, stating that addressing their situation is a humanitarian and national priority requiring practical and urgent measures. Finally, the participants agreed on the need to establish a common vision and an appropriate monitoring mechanism to ensure the implementation of all decisions.

author: Unknown
title: Two women sentenced to death over January protests in Iran
content:
For the first time in Iran, two women have been sentenced to death in connection with the anti-regime protests in January. The death sentences against 20-year-old Taraneh Rahimi and 43-year-old Leila Abolhasani were handed down in two separate trials in Isfahan. According to the Norway-based human rights organization Iran Human Rights (IHR), no woman had previously been executed in connection with the protest movement. By contrast, numerous death sentences against men have already been carried out. IHR puts the number of men executed for their participation in the protests at 29.


Taraneh Rahimi sentenced to death alongside nine men


Taraneh Rahimi was sentenced to death alongside nine men over events that took place in a square in Isfahan. Two people were killed in the incidents, including a member of the Revolutionary Guards. According to the human rights organization HRANA, other defendants were sentenced to lengthy prison terms. Among them is Rahimi’s sister, Romina, who was sentenced to 36 years in prison.


Both NGOs have criticized serious shortcomings in the proceedings. The defendants’ lawyers were reportedly denied access to large portions of the case files and were not given sufficient time to review the documents and evidence.


Leila Abolhasani and Taraneh Rahimi 


Death sentence over alleged arson


In a separate case, 43-year-old Leila Abolhasani was sentenced to death. The mother of two teenagers was convicted by a court in Isfahan of setting fire to a shop during the protests. Her family rejects the accusation, saying that Abolhasani had merely filmed the burning shop.


Her case was reported by HRANA and the human rights organization Dadban. According to the NGO Iran Human Rights (IHR), 16 women have also been sentenced to death and executed on other charges so far this year.


Protests left thousands dead


The protests began in late December 2025 amid a severe economic crisis and subsequently developed into nationwide mass demonstrations against the regime. They reached their peak on January 8 and 9.


Tehran later acknowledged that more than 3,000 people had been killed, but blamed the deaths on “acts of terrorism” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. Human rights organizations outside Iran, however, say the state violently suppressed the protests, resulting in more than twice that number of deaths.

title: August Community Time in the Gitigaan and Beyond
content:
August marks the beginning of the harvest season for many communities across northern Minnesota. While some of the early summer berries are beginning to wane, late-season fruits are coming on strong, with plums, apples, and other fruits beginning to ripen. Across the region, the landscape is shifting from the abundance of midsummer toward the gathering and preservation of foods and medicines that will sustain communities through the coming seasons.

August is also a significant time for manoomin/psin (wild rice). As the rice ripens across northern Minnesota and Wisconsin, community members are busy on the water gathering this culturally important staple food. Harvesting manoomin/psin is much more than gathering food—it is a practice that connects people to water, land, family, community, and generations of knowledge. The health of the rice beds is deeply connected to the health of the waters and the broader ecosystems that sustain them.

At the same time, water protectors and Indigenous communities across the North continue to stand up for the protection of manoomin/psin and the waters where it grows. Proposed and ongoing mining and pipeline projects pose serious concerns for wild rice waters, wildlife habitat, and the long-term health of Indigenous communities. Protecting manoomin/psin means protecting the waters and the relationships that have sustained communities for generations.

Here at the IEN Teaching Garden, our gitigaan is bursting with food, flowers, and medicines. Echinacea, elderberry, anise hyssop, and many other plants are thriving.

On August 29, the IEN Teaching Garden crew joined the local Bemidji Pride Festival at the Railriver Folk School in Bemidji, Minnesota. The annual festival takes place at the same community hub where the IEN Teaching Garden and IEN office are located, making it a natural opportunity to bring the garden and our land-based work into conversation with the broader community.

On August 29, the IEN Teaching Garden crew joined the local Bemidji Pride Festival at the Railriver Folk School in Bemidji, Minnesota. The annual festival takes place at the same community hub where the IEN Teaching Garden and IEN office are located, making it a natural opportunity to bring the garden and our land-based work into conversation with the broader community.

[Image: DJ Seki and volunteer Joe tabling at the Bemidji Pride Festival in the Gittigaan (IEN Teaching Garden) above on the left.]

IEN has maintained a longstanding relationship with the Bemidji Pride community and has supported local Pride efforts over the years. Our participation in the festival reflects the importance of building relationships across our community and creating spaces where people can come together, share knowledge, and celebrate one another.

Garden Associate DJ Seki and volunteer Joe helped staff the IEN Teaching Garden table throughout the event, connecting with festival participants and sharing information about the garden and its ongoing programs.

At the same time, Garden Manager Kaylee Carnahan welcomed visitors into the gitigaan and offered tours of the garden, giving community members an opportunity to see the food, medicines, pollinator habitat, and other projects growing throughout the space.

[Image: Wild rice in birch bark basket, above on the right.]

As summer begins to transition toward fall, August reminds us of the abundance that comes from healthy land and water—and of the responsibility we share to care for those places. From gathering manoomin/psin on the water to tending medicines in the gitigaan, these seasonal practices strengthen relationships, pass knowledge between generations, and help build a more resilient and food-sovereign community.

[Image: Echinacea and Elderberries, above center.]

title: Book Review: Courage or Complicity? How Veterans are Responding to the Assault on Democracy
content:
U.S. military veterans are drilled by their commanders to obey their superior officers. Many still believe it is their duty to support the commander-in-chief even after their tour of duty.


But at a time when Donald Trump is undermining the Veterans Administration, attacking unions and other democratic institutions, and instigating illegal wars, could the nation’s 17 million military veterans become key allies in the fight for workers’ rights, democracy, and peace?


In their recent book

Courage or Complicity? How Veterans are Responding to the Assault on Democracy

, Steve Early and Suzanne Gordon provide a wealth of examples showing how veterans and labor can form a powerful alliance for change.


The authors cite veterans like Richard Ojeda, a 25-year Army vet who voted for Bernie Sanders in the 2016 primary, and for Trump in the general election. But now, says Ojeda, people “are realizing that they were pawns in the oldest con game in the book—blame immigrants, blame workers, blame anyone who doesn’t look or pray… the way you do.”


Many vets feel bitter about the wars our leaders are sending them to, and wary of Trump’s war-mongering. Vietnam vet Jerry Lembcke observes that a lot of veterans “came back [from overseas] deflated and disappointed.” Another veteran concluded, “We were not guests, but invaders… we were occupiers.”


Veteran Daniel Sjursen decided that the war in Iraq was “built on lies, ill-advised, illegal, and immoral.” He now wants to find more “socially conscious veterans of these endless, fruitless wars who are willing to step up… for revitalized patriotic dissent.”


FIGHTING FOR THE VA


Instead of more wars, what many vets want from both the government and employers is support for their mental and physical needs.


As the authors note, veterans are at higher risk for post-traumatic stress disorder, substance abuse, and suicide. Even “joystick warriors” who carried out targeted assassinations via Hellfire missiless from the other side of the world have experienced PTSD.  One U.S. Air Force vet involved in drone operations suffered from “depression, sleep disorders, and anxiety.” Two of her former colleagues committed suicide.


Many vets are angry about Trump’s cuts and outsourcing at the Veterans Administration, which have led to staffing shortages and compromised treatment for vets in need. The Trump regime has cancelled nearly 600 federal contracts and proposed a $12 billion cut in funding for VA caregivers.


Early and Gordon write that close to one-third of the VA’s healthcare workforce—about 100,000 people—are veterans. “So at VA hospitals around the country, vets are taking care of other vets—as doctors, nurses, therapists, and support staff.” This, they write, “creates a real community of care which is not reproducible in a ‘fee for service’ world of privatized care that siphons off billions of dollars every year away from the VA budget.”


And yet the Trump administration is doing everything it can to privatize VA services and demolish federal unions representing staff at the VA and elsewhere.


In response to Trump’s efforts to partially privatize the VA, thousands of members of American Federation of Government Employees, National Nurses Union, and Veterans For Peace organized protests on a national “Day to Save the VA.”


Vets employed by the Department of Veterans Affairs have been campaigning to “Save Our VA,” with active support from Veterans for Peace and the veterans group Common Defense. Vets in the U.S. Postal Service (one of the nation’s largest employers of veterans) are also rank-and-file leaders in the fight against privatization.


Labor Notes has helped bring together VA patients and their caregivers to fight VA privatization. They’ve linked this to the fight for universal healthcare, noting that the VA can be a model of not-for-profit healthcare.  The Federal Unionists Network is organizing to fight cutbacks at all of the federal agencies.


VETERANS AS ORGANIZERS


Men and women in military service learn that they have to count on each other for survival. As Early and Gordon put it, “Their past experience with collective action can be put to good use in a strike situation or in a non-union workplace where organizers must be resourceful and brave to stand up to anti-union employers like Amazon or Walmart.”


And since many blue-collar communities hold veterans in high respect, vets can be an important asset for unions trying to generate popular support for their …

author: Julia Conley
title: Judge Strikes Down New York Law Requiring Polluters to Pay for Climate Change
content:
The landmark law would require oil and gas companies in the state to pay $75 billion toward a climate superfund.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Climate advocates on Monday called on New York Attorney General Letitia James to appeal a ruling by a federal judge that found the state’s superfund law, aimed at holding fossil fuel companies accountable for the weather disasters they cause, was unenforceable — “a bad decision,” as campaigner Jamie Henn said, “based off a controversial ruling.”

Henn, co-founder of 350.org and director of Fossil Free Media, said that “a cabal of Big Oil lawyers, Republican attorneys general, and Trump administration stooges just convinced a federal judge to strike down” the law, which was signed in 2024 by Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul and would require oil and gas companies in New York to contribute about $3 billion annually — $75 billion total — to a superfund starting in 2028.

That sum would be divided among the companies according to their greenhouse gas emissions, which cause planetary heating and the hurricanes, flooding, and other extreme weather disasters that are associated with it.

Companies that have been found responsible for at least 1 billion tons of fossil fuel emissions between 2000-18 would be required to contribute to the fund, which would be used to rebuild infrastructure and help communities adapt to more frequent extreme weather events.

Chief Judge Brenda Sannes of the US District Court for the Northern District of New York ruled that a federal appeals court’s earlier decision in City of New York v. Chevron Corp., in which the city’s lawsuit against oil companies for climate damages was thrown out, was relevant to the Climate Change Superfund Act.

Sannes, who was appointed by former President Barack Obama, also said in her ruling that the state law is not authorized by the Clean Air Act and is preempted by federal law.

Henn said that after 22 Republican states joined industry groups and the US Chamber of Commerce in suing over the law, the judge “fell for Big Oil’s argument that because of a precedent set by a controversial ruling involving the City of New York, the superfund program was preempted by the Clean Air Act.”

“But that’s bogus,” said Henn. “The superfund program does nothing to regulate future emissions, it’s just asking polluters to pay for a small share of the damages caused by their past pollution.”

A cabal of Big Oil lawyers, Republican AGs, and Trump Administration stooges just convinced a federal judge to strike down New York's "Climate Superfund" Law. This is a bad decision, based off a controversial ruling, and should be immediately appealed. It will do nothing to…

A judge in Vermont is expected to rule soon on the state’s superfund law, which was the first in the nation. Sixteen states in all have proposed similar laws.

“This is far from the last word on the legality of climate superfund bills,” said Henn.

Maya Golden-Krasner, deputy director of the Climate Law Institute at the Center for Biological Diversity, urged other states to “move forward with fair legislation that makes polluters pay for their damage.”

“With the Trump administration gutting climate protections,” she said, the campaign for superfund laws in states including California “is gaining momentum every day” despite the legal setback.

“If allowed to stand, this wrongheaded ruling would shift $75 billion in planned climate-resilience funding from major fossil fuel polluters onto New York taxpayers,” said Golden-Krasner.

Henn also said that the push to hold fossil fuel giants accountable for the damages their emissions cause “isn’t going away.”

“Eighty percent of voters think the fossil fuel industry should pay their fair share of climate damages,” said Henn. “As disasters increase (and oil profits keep skyrocketing), the call to make polluters pay will only grow louder.”

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Dog attacks spur warning from Department of Health
content:
The Department of Health is reminding Nunavummiut to stay safe around dogs, citing “several” recent attacks across the territory.


The department published a public service announcement Monday afternoon, advising residents to “be aware of the risks” and asking “parents to have conversations with their children about safe interactions with dogs.”


“Any dog can bite,” spokesperson Charmaine Deogracias wrote in the announcement.


Citing privacy concerns, Deogracias declined to share with Nunatsiaq News where the the recent incidents occurred or how severe they were.


An 11-year-old girl was

medevaced last week with serious injuries

 to her head and face after a dog attacked her in Iqaluit.


The Department of Health announcement advises Nunavummiut to stay away from stray dogs, mothers and their pups, or dogs that are eating. It also says not to disturb a sleeping dog and to ask permission before petting a dog.


Due to the risk of rabies, anyone who gets bitten or scratched by a dog should wash the wound with soap and water, then go to their local health centre, according to the statement.

author: Simon Childs
title: Congressman Accuses Ex-Prince Andrew of Committing Sex Crimes in US
content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor perpetrated sex crimes in the US, a congressman has said.


Speaking in the chamber of the US House of Representatives on Tuesday, Thomas Massie, a Republican representative from Kentucky,

called for an investigation

 into the former prince and other prominent figures in the wake of revelations in the Epstein files. 


“We want perpetrators of these crimes to be investigated and prosecuted,” Massie said.


He then named a list of alleged perpetrators, which included, “Prince Andrew, who committed sex crimes in the United States.”


He added: “Perhaps hearing these names will shame the Department of Justice into delivering justice.” 


Massie was calling for a second Epstein files transparency act, claiming that US president Donald Trump’s administration “continues to withhold over three million files”.


Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his royal titles in October last year. He has repeatedly denied committing sex offences or any wrongdoing.


In February he was

arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office

 after files released by the US Department of Justice appeared to show he had shared sensitive government documents and commercial information with Epstein while working as trade envoy. He was released under investigation the same day. 


The ex-Prince has also been accused of sexually abusing one of Epstein’s trafficking victims, Virginia Giuffre. He paid her a settlement in 2022, made without admitting any liability. He continues to deny the allegation and has denied ever meeting Giuffre.

author: Unknown
title: İran Meclis Başkanı Kalibaf: "Hürmüz Boğazı'nın tam kontrolü silahlı kuvvetlerimizin elinde
content:
Fotoğraf: Mohammad Hassanzadeh/Wikimedia Commons CC BY 4.0

İran Meclis Başkanı Muhammed Bakır Kalibaf, ABD'nin birkaç gemiyi boğazdan geçirmeye çalıştığını fakat İran Silahlı Kuvvetlerinin müdahalesiyle karşılaşılaştıklarını söyledi.

Kalibaf, sosyal medya hesabından paylaştığı görüntülü konuşmasında Hürmüz Boğazı’ndaki son duruma ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu.

"Hürmüz Boğazı’nın tam kontrolü silahlı kuvvetlerimizin elindedir." diyen Kalibaf, ABD’nin Hürmüz Boğazı’ndan bazı gemileri geçirmeye çalıştığını savundu.

Kalibaf, "ABD, hırsızlar ve kaçakçılar gibi birkaç gemiyi boğazdan geçirmeye çalışıyor ancak silahlı kuvvetlerimizin müdahalesiyle karşılaşıyor." ifadelerini kullandı.

ABD'nin İran'a yönelik son saldırılarının Hürmüz Boğazı’nda İran'ın "gücünü kullanmasından" kaynaklandığını savunan Kalibaf, bu saldırılara "ağır karşılık" verdiklerini ileri sürdü.

Kalibaf, "Eğer boğazın kontrolü ABD’nin elindeyse, neden her gün bunu tekrarlamak ve adalarımıza saldırmak zorunda kalıyor?" dedi.

ABD’nin gemilere Hürmüz Boğazı’ndan geçebilecekleri yönünde güvence verdiğini ancak bu gemilerin saldırıya uğradığını ileri süren Kalibaf, "ABD, mutabakatın aksine boğazın güney güzergahını kullanmaya çalışıyor. Buna izin vermeyeceğiz." şeklinde konuştu.

Savaştan önce Hürmüz Boğazı’ndan günde en az 120 geminin geçtiğini ifade eden Kalibaf, "Bir veya iki geminin bile boğazdan geçmesi, savaş öncesi dönemle kesinlikle kıyaslanamaz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.

İran’ın Hürmüz Boğazı üzerindeki yönetiminin uluslararası hukukla çelişmediğini öne süren Kalibaf, son 15 ayda askeri alanda 10 yıllık ilerleme kaydettiklerini iddia etti.

Ateşkesin ardından farklı ülkelerdeki ABD üslerine yönelik saldırıların "stratejik anlam" taşıdığını belirten Kalibaf, İran’ın füze kapasitesinin düşman tarafından engellenemeyeceği mesajını verdiklerini belirtti.

Deniz ablukasının "askeri savaş" anlamına geldiğini yineleyen Kalibaf, düşmanın "hibrit savaş" kapsamında İran içinde protestoları terör ve kısa süreli askeri saldırılarla eş zamanlı olarak başlatmayı hedeflediğini söyledi.

İran İslam Cumhuriyeti'nin politikasının ülke lideri Mücteba Hamaney'in talimatı doğrultusunda mutabakatın şartlarının yerine getirilmesi olduğunu dile getiren Kalibaf, şunları kaydetti:

"Toplumsal bütünlük, birbirimize tavsiye etmemiz gereken en önemli toplumsal iyiliktir. Her kesimden tüm siyasetçilerden anlaşmazlıkları bir kenara bırakmalarını istiyorum. Gücümüzü ortaya koyarak mantığımızı düşmana kabul ettireceğiz ve hiçbir zaman askeri ya da siyasi olarak teslim olmayacağız."

title: Ακόμα μια κρατική δολοφονία από χέρια αστυνομικών στα Χανιά
content:
Στις 26/8 στο Α.Τ. Χανίων, οι μπάτσοι δολοφόνησαν τον Asraph. Άμεσα οι μηχανισμοί συγκάλυψης ξεκίνησαν να παίρνουν θέση, με τα ΜΜΕ 

να

 κάνουν λόγο για αυτοκτονία 

αναπαράγο

ντας

 τον λόγο των μπάτσων, προετοιμάζοντας έτσι το έδαφος για μια ακόμα συγκάλυψη κρατικής δολοφονίας. Ο Asraph ξυλοκοπήθηκε, βασανίστηκε και του αρνήθηκε η ιατροφαρμακευτική περίθαλψη μέσα στα κρατητήρια – κολαστήρια- όταν την ζήτησε. Η προσπάθεια συγκάλυψης της δολοφονίας του δεν μας ξαφνιάζει, γνωρίζουμε αρκετά καλά πως μέσα σε αυτά τα κολαστήρια κανένα δεν πεθαίνει τυχαία. Ξυλοδαρμοί, βιασμοί και βασανισμοί είναι πάγιες πρακτικές των μπάτσων δολοφόνων. Τα τμήματα ήταν ανέκαθεν χώροι όπου οι εξουσιαστές μπορούν να δρουν αυθαίρετα έχοντας μηχανισμούς που τους προσφέρουν ασυλία για τη βία που ασκούν.


Την Παρασκευή 28/8 έγινε δημόσια ενημέρωση της υπόθεσης στην εκδήλωση, που πραγματοποιούταν στο πλαίσιο του τριημέρου μνήμης και δράσεων για τα τρία χρόνια από την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη στον λόφο καστέλι όπου και καλούσε τον κόσμο σε αντανακλαστική πορεία το ίδιο βράδυ. Τρία χρόνια μετά, ερχόμαστε αντιμέτωπα με μια ακόμα κρατική δολοφονία και μια καλά συντονισμένη προσπάθεια συγκάλυψης, με τους μπάτσους να διατηρούν με συνέπεια τον ρόλο του δολοφόνου.


Με την λήξη της εκδήλωσης, δεκάδες συντρόφια συγκεντρώθηκαν έξω από την Κατειλημμένη Πρυτανεία όπου και ξεκίνησε η πορεία προς το ΑΤ Χανίων. Κατά την διάρκεια της πορείας φωνάχτηκαν συνθήματα με σκοπό να κάνουν γνωστή την υπόθεση στο κέντρο των Χανίων.


Το σώμα της πορείας στάθηκε μπροστά από το μπατσομέγαρο για κάποια ώρα, όπου φωνάχτηκαν συνθήματα προς τους μπάτσους δολοφόνους κάνοντας ξεκάθαρο πως καμία κρατική δολοφονία δεν θα μείνει αναπάντητη.

author: Chris Walker
title: Fetterman Backs Trump’s Insulting Comments Berating Opponents of Data Centers
content:
Fetterman’s comments come as Trump describes those opposed to expanding data centers as “backwards.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Right-leaning Democratic Party Sen. John Fetterman (Pennsylvania) has expressed support for the expansion of data centers, despite bipartisan pushback against their construction.

Fetterman’s remarks came on Monday following President Donald Trump’s post on Truth Social deriding Americans who have organized in opposition to the building of data centers.

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote. “If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

Fetterman — who has expressed support for many Trump-led initiatives since being elected senator and is reportedly being courted by Republicans to switch parties — also stated his support for the expansion of data center construction.

In a post on X, Fetterman reacted positively to a Bloomberg report on Trump’s post by writing, “Agreed,” and adding, “We must win the war for AI supremacy over China.” He also suggested that he understood the political ramifications of his statement.

“There’s nothing more damaging to a Democrat than agreeing with Trump AND data centers,” Fetterman wrote. But he claimed his position is still the “right” one to stake.

Support for data centers isn’t just damaging to Democrats, as Fetterman has recognized — it’s a position that has bipartisan opposition.

According to a Fox News poll published in July, only 30 percent of respondents said they would support a data center being built in their area, while 70 percent opposed the idea. Sixty percent of Republicans opposed the construction of data centers near them, while 76 percent of Democrats were opposed.

Others reacted to Trump’s post less enthusiastically than Fetterman did. Chris Deluzio, a Democratic congressman who is also from Pennsylvania, condemned the president’s comments on data centers.

Trump’s post is “so disrespectful to people who have concerns about AI’s roles in our lives, or electricity costs, or whether good union jobs are part of this, or water supplies — you name it,” Deluzio said in a video post. “It certainly isn’t because they want to be backwards and poor.”

The construction of data centers across multiple states, particularly those used for AI systems, has led to grassroots resistance, with opponents voicing concerns over environmental impacts, rising costs of utility bills for regular consumers, air and noise pollution, and other issues. Those arguing in favor of regulation of such centers have also noted labor concerns regarding the expansion of AI centers.

“AI in the hands of the transnational capitalist class is an instrument of class warfare against the global working and popular classes,” explained William I. Robinson, professor of sociology at the University of California at Santa Barbara, writing for Truthout in an op-ed published in June. “AI accelerates the process whereby labor is deskilled, made precarious, and expelled through algorithmic restructuring of the labor process and outright automation.”

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Iqaluit artist brings Nunavut cross country through tissue boxes
content:
The view from Iqaluit artist Yurak’s Apex window is making its way into Canadian homes, one tissue box at a time.


Iqaluit artist Yurak holds two Royale tissue boxes showing the reverse sides of

Brilliance Beyond the Horizon

 and

Tuktuliaq

. The two designs are featured in Royale’s Canadian Artist Collection. (Photo by Mosha Folger)


The design,

Brilliance Beyond the Horizon

, shows a frozen landscape and waters of Frobisher Bay. It’s one of two designs that Yurak, the pen name of Siku Rojas, created for Royale, a Canadian household paper-products brand, as part of the company’s new Canadian Artist Collection.


The limited-edition collection features eight designs by five artists from across the country, each asked to interpret what home means to them through the theme The View From Here.


“I think that’s the lovely thing about this campaign, is that they want to show that Canada is so vast and we’re a very multicultural country,” Yurak said.


Last winter, a public relations agency working with Royale asked Yurak to participate in the collection.

The multi-media artist completed the project before January.


Rather than create separate illustrations for each side of the box, Yurak drew one wrap-around piece.


“What I was trying to do is consider what I wanted the rest of Canada to know about my ideas of home, of Nunavut, and not even just what everyday life is, but what our aspirations are,” they said.


The first design,

Brilliance Beyond the Horizon

, is a snapshot of the landscape outside Yurak’s home.


“I really wanted viewers, and Inuit who are seeing my art, to also consider what is beyond the horizon and what more beautiful things can we do,” they said.


The flipside features fireweed, purple saxifrage — Nunavut’s territorial flower — and Arctic heather, as well as berries and other plants harvested for food.


The artwork also includes cultural tattoos and beadwork, which Yurak said represent the skills and crafts that Nunavummiut contribute to Canada.


The second design,

Tuktuliak,

which is

caribou hunting in Inuktitut, depicts where Yurak hunted with family last September and harvested a caribou for the first time, about two hours outside Iqaluit.


“I’m always trying to reopen minds and to keep reminding the rest of the world of the importance of hunting, because I know oftentimes people have a negative feeling towards it,” Yurak said.


Both pieces were created on an iPad. Royale provided a colour scheme, but Yurak added additional colours, including reds in

Tuktuliak

 to reflect the fall landscape.


“I really wanted to keep it being colourful for these boxes to, again, remove that white snow slate that people depict,” Yurak said.


The finished boxes arrived at Yurak’s home a couple of weeks ago, and the response has been positive so far.


“Everyone’s wanting access to it and wondering where to purchase it,” Yurak said. “People are saying that they even want to keep reusing it, which is very funny.”


The Royale Canadian Artist Collection will be available this month at Home Hardware locations in Rankin Inlet and Arviat and can also be ordered online through Amazon and other retailers.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Tras las críticas de Andrés Rodríguez, Aguiar lo desafió a fijar una fecha de paro conjunto en la administración pública para “romper el techo salarial”
content:
“Le pedimos que reflexione y se sume a la pelea. Si eso sucede, tal vez los resultados que se obtengan sean bastante distintos. Está preocupado porque fue oficialista con todos los gobiernos, pero en el fondo sabe que con Milei es distinto porque, cuando caiga Milei, él también va a caer y será su derrumbe definitivo”, indicó Rodolfo Aguiar, dirigente de ATE.


El Secretario General de ATE Nacional, Rodolfo Aguiar, respondió a los cuestionamientos del líder de UPCN, Andrés Rodríguez y señaló: “Le pedimos que reflexione y se sume a la pelea. Si eso sucede, tal vez los resultados que se obtengan sean bastante distintos”.


El dirigente de UPCN había cuestionado a Aguiar en declaraciones radiales por “hacerse el combativo y no obtener mejoras salariales”. Ante esa situación, el dirigente de ATE respondió: “Si convocamos juntos a una huelga en el Estado Nacional, en las provincias y municipios, entonces podremos saber si son los trabajadores los que no están dispuestos a luchar como dice Rodríguez o, en realidad, es UPCN la funcional al Gobierno por aceptar recurrentemente sus migajas”.


En esta línea, Aguiar afirmó: “La respuesta de un dirigente que reconoce que todos los sectores están perdiendo poder adquisitivo en las paritarias no puede tener como respuesta quedarse durmiendo la siesta en su casa”.


“En el fondo, Rodríguez muestra resignación y tiene miedo de perder todos sus privilegios. Fue oficialista con todos los gobiernos, pero sabe que con Milei es distinto porque, cuando caiga Milei, él también va a caer y será su derrumbe definitivo”, dijo, y agregó: “Desde ATE, nuestros delegados tienen que responder con más afiliaciones. Esta reacción destemplada solo puede entenderse de alguien que está cerca de perder su representación mayoritaria”.


En este contexto, el dirigente gremial dijo: “Si de verdad Rodríguez está preocupado por el deterioro de los ingresos del sector público, otro buen paso sería que dejen de extorsionar y empobrecer a los trabajadores cobrando coseguros ilegales en la obra social“.


“Todos recordamos que Menem les regaló una obra social que era de todos los trabajadores y hoy nos damos cuenta que no tienen la capacidad y no están preparados para administrar. Si siguen así, la van a chocar”, afirmó.


En este contexto, Aguiar concluyó: “Ojalá se decidan por la unidad en acción. Hoy más que nunca enfrentamos una lucha de clases. Hay que poner todo, cuerpo y alma. La historia nos vuelve a dividir entre los que luchan y los que se entregan, y la unidad tiene que ser con aquellos con los que están dispuestos a dar pelea”.


Cabe destacar que en la última paritaria, el Gobierno ofreció un 1,9% en septiembre, 1,8% en octubre, 1,6% en noviembre y 1,5% en diciembre, además de una suma fija de $80.000 no remunerativa por única vez para el último mes del año.


Además, desde que asumió Javier Milei, el poder de compra de los estatales cayó más de un 44% en todo el país, producto de las sistemáticas paritarias aceptadas por UPCN y rechazadas por ATE.


En este marco, ATE realizó decenas, movilizaciones y jornadas nacionales de lucha en todos los ministerios y organismos públicos durante la gestión del gobierno libertario para exigir mejoras en rechazo a los despidos, por mejoras en las condiciones laborales y aumentos salariales.

author: James Green
title: As 10 medidas de Trump para tentar vencer as eleições de novembro nos EUA
content:
O presidente Trump não esconde um de seus maiores medos: perder o controle republicano do Congresso dos EUA em 3 de novembro, o que possivelmente levaria a um

terceiro processo de impeachment

. No entanto, sua resposta é uma mistura caótica de medidas para evitar uma derrota avassaladora que poderia, de fato, concretizar seu cenário de pesadelo.


Quais são seus planos para uma vitória eleitoral? Quais condições ele criou que podem levar à sua ruína política durante os dois últimos anos de seu governo? 


As

pesquisas

 mostram consistentemente uma taxa de impopularidade geral de Trump em torno de 63%, contra uma de aprovação de cerca de 35%, composta em grande parte por seus apoiadores leais do movimento MAGA.

As duas principais questões para os eleitores continuam sendo a inflação — com o aumento dos custos de alimentos, combustíveis, fertilizantes e moradia — e a guerra contra o Irã, sem qualquer desfecho positivo visível para o governo Trump.

 A atual composição do Congresso confere aos republicanos uma maioria mínima de quatro cadeiras tanto na Câmara quanto no Senado, o que significa que qualquer pequena mudança na preferência dos eleitores poderia transferir o poder para os democratas nas eleições de novembro.


Plano A: redesenhar o mapa das eleições nos EUA


O plano inicial de Trump para derrotar os democratas consistia em pressionar as maiorias republicanas nas legislaturas de vários estados a redesenhar os limites dos distritos eleitorais para favorecer seu partido

,

realocando

 prováveis eleitores democratas para distritos com maioria republicana e, assim, diluindo sua força nas urnas.


Simultaneamente, os seis membros da Suprema Corte dos EUA nomeados por republicanos esvaziaram dispositivos fundamentais da histórica

Lei de Direitos de Voto de 1965

. Eles decidiram que levar em conta padrões históricos de discriminação racial contra eleitores negros não justificava mais medidas destinadas a proteger o peso do voto afro-americano nas eleições dos estados do Sul.


Dada a recente polarização política nos Estados Unidos, na qual a maioria dos 435 distritos da Câmara foi desenhada para favorecer um partido em detrimento do outro, as estimativas atuais apontam, pelo menos, para

49 distritos

 nos quais há uma disputa real entre candidatos republicanos e democratas pela representação no Congresso. Pesquisas também indicam que, em nível nacional, os democratas detêm

uma vantagem de 6% a 7%

 sobre os republicanos, o que sugere que provavelmente conquistarão o controle da Câmara dos Representantes.


A situação no Senado é mais complexa, pois os democratas precisarão reeleger vários titulares e conquistar cadeiras em estados que apoiaram candidatos presidenciais republicanos nas últimas décadas — Alasca, Carolina do Norte, Iowa, Ohio, Texas e Maine —, embora as pesquisas atuais favoreçam os

candidatos democratas

 nestes estados por margens estreitas.


O plano B: cortar eleitores da lista


Após não conseguir assegurar uma possível maioria republicana por meio do redesenho dos mapas distritais,

a estratégia seguinte de Trump foi emitir ordens executivas destinadas a restringir o voto de prováveis apoiadores de candidatos democratas, assumindo o controle federal sobre o processo eleitoral nacional

 — uma responsabilidade claramente atribuída aos estados pela Constituição dos EUA.


O pretexto utilizado é a suposta ocorrência generalizada de votos de não cidadãos, argumento que se alinha convenientemente à campanha agressiva de Trump contra imigrantes, mantida há uma década. No entanto, todas as investigações confiáveis sobre possíveis votos ilegais de não cidadãos revelam um

número ínfimo de pessoas que efetivamente violaram a lei

. Tal fato jamais determinou a vitória ou a derrota de um candidato em qualquer disputa eleitoral.


Perda do controle dos Republicanos no Congresso pode abrir caminho para novos processos de

impeachment

 contra Trump


Terceiro plano: pressionar governadores democratas


A

terceira

 iniciativa de Trump

consistiu

 em

exigir que governadores de estados com tendência democrata repassassem ao governo federal informações de registro eleitoral, para que este pudesse determinar quais eleitores registrados eram elegíveis para votar.


Isso conferiria ao Departamento de Segurança Interna poder ilimitado para definir quem seria considerado um eleitor legítimo e quem, na sua visão, não seria elegível ao voto. Até o momento, governadores democratas recusaram-se a …

author: Unknown
title: KJK: Our people in Rojava must never accept education that is not in their mother tongue
content:
The Coordination of the Communities of Women of Kurdistan (KJK) said in a statement: "On 27 August, the Syrian Ministry of Education announced its decision regarding the implementation of Decree No. 13 issued by the Syrian Presidency. Although the decision defines Kurdish as a national language, limiting Kurdish-language education to a few classes of three to four hours per week reveals an approach aimed at undermining and eliminating the gains achieved by the people. It is unacceptable to address the right of the Kurdish people, who constitute the second-largest population in Syria, to education in their own language in this way. The designation of a national language refers to an official language, and this also means that it is granted official status as a mother tongue. To call it a national language while not granting it official-language status is contrary to both the law and the realities of life."


The right to mother tongue education is non-negotiable


The KJK added: "Mother tongue is the expression, through words and meaning, of a people’s identity, character, history, traditions, and way of making sense of life,” the KJK statement said, adding: “Every restriction placed on a mother tongue means nothing more than an attempt to sever people from their sense of self and their collective memory. In this sense, the right to speak one’s mother tongue, receive education in it, and live according to it is such a vital right that it cannot even be a subject of debate. Therefore, this practice does not only mean obstructing the Kurdish people; it also means obstructing the struggle to build a democratic Syria in which all peoples and identities can participate with their own colors. Because democratic integration does not mean forcing people to accept assimilation, it is a struggle to establish the most common foundations necessary for democratic regimes to emerge and to build a system upon them. It absolutely does not mean accepting the impositions of one side."


The KJK continued: "For a century, our people in Rojava have stubbornly maintained their self-defense against the imposed denial of their identity, first by insisting on preserving their culture and language. After Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] went to Rojava in 1979, they participated in the freedom struggle by giving everything they had, and ultimately, through the Rojava Revolution, they tore away the denial of their identity. For a long time, they have developed a system of living and governing themselves with their own identity and character within the unity of Syria, and have developed their education system accordingly. For approximately twelve years, they have conducted educational activities from primary school through university and have graduated thousands of children and young people. In this sense, they have demonstrated to the whole world that bilingual education and life are possible, that this is a source of richness for a country, and that it does not lead to fragmentation or division. Behind the hope that Rojava has inspired around the world as a model lies these realities demonstrated by the system it has established. It is clear that a people that has paid such a high price and struggled to preserve its identity, and has transformed the reasons for its struggle into an established system, can never accept this imposed practice. The justified reactions expressed by Kongra Star, students, and academic circles are an important reflection of how our people in Rojava approach this issue."


Our people in Rojava must express their opposition anywhere


The KJK underlined that "the designation of Kurdish as a national language in the Syrian presidential decree, which has no binding force in an official sense, amounts to little more than an attempt to put forward such a provision in order to soften these reactions. In this sense, our people in Rojava must not accept this practice under any circumstances and must express their justified opposition everywhere and in every form. They must develop a campaign of democratic resistance in order to ensure that the existing decisions are changed on a democratic basis.


Students in Rojava must fully defend their right to receive education in their own language. They must defend the major achievements of the people of Rojava over more than a decade, say “we will never accept education that is not in our mother tongue,” and demonstrate in practice that they will not accept any other arrangement. author: Unknown
title: On 1 September - Anti-War Day: The Kurdish struggle against the logic of war
content:
In a written statement marking 1 September World Peace Day,


the Executive Council of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) said the following:


“To mark Anti-War Day, at this time when there is hardly any talk of peace but constant discussion of war and acts of aggression, we want to use the example of the Kurdish Freedom Movement to show that peace is possible.  


One of the main centres of conflict is the Middle East, where it is possible to draw up a long list of conflicts including the longstanding war in Palestine, the war involving Iran, the USA, Israel, Yemen, and Lebanon, the instability in Syria and Iraq, and the shift in the Turkish state’s position. 


Efforts to pursue the alternative – to pursue peace – are a rarity. The exception in the Middle East is the political campaign for peace led by the Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan and his movement.


After 47 years of armed struggle against the assimilation and annihilation of the Kurdish people by the Turkish state, on 27 February 2025, Öcalan radically challenged the regional and international logic of war with his call for Peace and a Democratic Society. 


Since the founding of the Republic in 1923, Turkey has consistently relied on aggression and militarism. All political struggles for freedom and equality in society were countered by the Turkish state, including with three military coups (1960, 1971, 1980).  The Kurds were forced to turn to self-defence, to ensure their survival.  Despite state aggression, the Kurds have managed not only to survive, but also to voice their demands beyond Turkey’s borders. No state authority has succeeded in breaking the Kurdish people’s high level of organisation and mobility. Kurdish society, characterised by women’s freedom and the coexistence of diversity, has created a strong understanding of democracy. It is a society that, through its political resistance, can bring about democracy and, consequently, peace even beyond national borders.


Öcalan’s radical break with the previous form of resistance draws on the strength of Kurdish society and the values it has forged, but also on the realisation that the Turkish state has reached the end of its war logic, which has failed to defeat the Kurds. The realisation on the part of the Turkish state, brought about by Öcalan’s struggle, could become a prime example for the entire Middle East region. If Turkey, Syria and Iran were to adopt Kurdish proposals for a solution –the democratic integration of the Kurds into a democratised political system and legal framework– this could bring new hope to the entire region. 


Resolving the Kurdish question could bring peace to the Middle East. International support for Öcalan’s efforts is crucial.


For this to happen:


The criminalisation of the Kurds through the inclusion of the PKK on the EU and US terrorist lists, and the ban on the PKK in Germany, must be lifted so that Kurds can freely pursue their political struggle for democracy and peace.


The Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe must implement Öcalan's right to hope by taking practical steps.”

author: Unknown
title: Guerrillas: Öcalan’s call for peace should not be exploited and every day should be a day of peace
content:
Speaking to ANF on the occasion of September 1, World Peace Day, YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) guerrillas in the Medya Defense Zones said that the past century, marked by war and chaos, could evolve into a peaceful and democratic century through the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan.


Wars in the Middle East achieved no gains and no resolution


YJA Star guerrilla Avaşîn Dîcle stated that hegemonic powers have incited peoples against one another as the Middle East has been subjected to wars and conflicts for the past century. She said:


“As is well known, the Middle East as a whole has been marked by war for the past century. Hegemonic powers and their partners have subjected the Middle East to war and conflict. When we look at the reality of these wars, we see nations and peoples being incited against one another and made to kill each other. The peoples of the region have suffered immensely as a result of these wars. Forced displacement, destroyed cities and massacres have been inflicted upon the peoples of the Middle East.


Ultimately, these have been wars with no gains and no resolution. The Kurdish people, in particular, have been among those most affected by these wars. For this reason, the Kurds have faced some of the worst massacres, experienced firsthand the devastation caused by war, and learned to distinguish between war and peace. In this sense, we can say that the Kurdish people are among those who yearn most deeply for peace.”


The parties must engage in direct dialogue in order to achieve a lasting solution


The YJA Star guerrilla pointed out that Abdullah Öcalan’s previous peace initiatives had been exploited and stated that the parties must engage in direct dialogue in order to achieve a lasting solution.


“We believe that if a problem is to be resolved, the process must be bilateral. Those who are fighting each other are the ones who can understand this best. This is a reality known to the parties concerned. The involvement of a third party means using the situation for its own interests. In particular, a third party will only deepen the conflict,” Dîcle said, continuing:


“Because the Leader saw and analyzed this situation, he called on democratic societies and the peoples of the region in general to pursue a resolution through dialogue. This is a call for a path toward a solution, and it encompasses every society. In fact, it encompasses all peoples who want to achieve something in the Middle East. To respond to the current call, it is of course necessary to understand and embrace it.


No solution has been reached so far as Öcalan's former peaceful initiatives were exploited


As guerrillas loyal to the Leader, we see that a process of dialogue has been initiated with the Turkish state, but no solution has yet been reached. This is not the first time the Leader has undertaken peaceful initiatives. In the past, he both declared ceasefires and opened the door to peace. However, these initiatives were exploited by the enemy and used for different purposes. They were used to serve their own interests, with the aim of suppressing and eliminating the guerrilla forces. We cannot say that they approached these initiatives with much sincerity. As a result, not only was no solution reached, but the war also continued.


Many of our wounds inflicted by the state are still fresh. There are burned villages and countless people who fell victims to unsolved killings. There have been countless instances of forced displacement and massacres. There was even a peace process initiated by the Leader, yet attacks and massacres against Rojava took place. For this reason, we have doubts about the state. Nevertheless, the Leader has initiated a process, and we want to embrace and support it.


Turkish people manipulated by those in power through nationalist sentiments


In this context, we know that the Turkish people, in particular, have been manipulated by those in power through nationalist sentiments. For nearly a century, the Kurdish people have been branded as ‘terrorists,’ and under the pretext of ‘fighting against them,’ the people have been subjected to hunger and deprived of their will. In fact, the Turkish people need peace even more than we do. In this sense, if the Turkish people embrace this process, it can move forward in a positive direction.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Jorge Macri ataca al sindicato Ademys por luchar contra el BA Aprende”
content:
El Gobierno de la Ciudad inició una causa penal contra Soledad Mosquera, Secretaria General del sindicato docente Ademys, y otros dos miembros de su Comisión Directiva por haber ido a acompañar la lucha de la comunidad educativa de la escuela Niní Marshall contra la regresiva reforma educativa denominada BA Aprende.”Es un intento burdo y bruto – es Jorge Macri, no se puede esperar otra cosa- de aleccionar a docentes y estudiantes”, señalaron desde el gremio.


Compartimos el comunicado:


Jorge Macri ataca al sindicato Ademys por luchar contra el BA Aprende


El gobierno inició una causa Penal contra nuestra Secretaria General, Soledad Mosquera; la Secretaria de Derechos Humanos, Vanesa Gagliardi; y a Eugenio Ariza, miembro del Consejo Directivo actual. ¿Por qué? Porque fueron a acompañar la lucha de estudiantes, familias y docentes de la escuela Nini Marshall contra el BA Aprende. Vanesa es docente de la Nini y forma parte del colectivo docente que se planta contra esta reforma regresiva.


Es un intento burdo y bruto – es Jorge Macri, no se puede esperar otra cosa- de aleccionar a docentes y estudiantes que enfrentan el BA Aprende. Quieren que Ademys “baje el copete” y se retire de las luchas.


Lo decimos claramente: no va a pasar, vamos a redoblar nuestro esfuerzo y compromiso en defensa de la escuela pública.


Es lamentable la torpeza del gobierno que, perdido en su interna con los libertarios, se lanza contra el sindicato combativo y democrático de CABA.


Esta no es la primera vez que el gobierno judicializa a miembros de nuestro sindicato, sino que es una política sistemática de persecución al único sindicato docente que actúa como oposición a los distintos gobiernos del macrismo. Nos persigue porque denunciamos las políticas anti educativas del macrismo y rechazamos los acuerdos salariales o laborales -porque son todos regresivos, la docencia lo sabe-.


Abajo la causa trucha contra Ademys y contra quienes defienden la educación pública.


Llamamos al resto de los sindicatos a pronunciarse en este sentido. Tocan a unx, tocan a todxs.


Nos vemos en las calles.

author: Unknown
title: "Batık gemi olduğu değerlendirilen cisim 550 metrede tespit edildi"
content:
Kuzey Kıbrıs Türk Cumhuriyeti (KKTC) Cumhurbaşkanı Tufan Erhürman, Girne Limanı’nda kurulan “Kriz Masası” önünde arama-kurtarma çalışmalarına ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu.


KKTC Başbakanı Ünal Üstel’le birlikte çalışmaları yerinde gözlemlediklerini belirten Erhürman “Şu anda batık gemi olduğu değerlendirilen cismin yeri 550 metrede tespit edildi” dedi.


Çok teknik ve çok hassas yürütülen bir çalışma var. Dolayısıyla yavaş ilerliyor. Yavaş ilerlediği için de çok kısa sürede sonuç alamıyoruz.

– KKTC Cumhurbaşkanı Tufan Erhürman


KKTC Başbakanı Üstel’in açıklamasına göre, gemideki 267 kişiden 239’u kurtarıldı, 8 kişi hayatını kaybetti. Kayıp 20 kişi için arama-kurtarma çalışmaları üçüncü gününde sürüyor.


Alemdar gemisi çalışmalara katılacak


Erhürman, Türk Deniz Kuvvetleri’ne bağlı kurtarma gemisi TCG Alemdar’ın yarın (2 Eylül) sabah itibarıyla arama-kurtarma çalışmalarına katılacağını açıkladı.


TCG Alemdar’ın gece çalışma teknolojisine sahip olduğunu belirten Erhürman, “Deniz yüzeyindeki çalışma da aralıksız devam ediyor. Dalgıçların 90 metreden öteye inmesi mümkün değil. 550 metre derinlikte çalışma yapılması hiç kolay bir iş değil” ifadelerini kullandı.


FİLO JET GEMİ KAZASI


Girne açıklarında kaybolan 20 kişiyi arama çalışmaları sürüyor


Bugün  13:35


Kayıp yakınından Erhürman’a tepki


Kazadan sağ kurtulan ancak iki çocuğu hala kayıp durumda olan Ayten Biçer, açıklama sırasında Erhürman’a tepki gösterdi.


Biçer, “Biz çocuklarımızı bekliyoruz, siz televizyona açıklama yapıyorsunuz. Bana açıklama yapacaksınız, göstermelik iş yapıyorsunuz” dedi.


Erhürman ise “Öfkenizi anlıyorum, çok haklısınız. Biraz sonra yanınıza geleceğim” yanıtı verdi.


Girne’deki feribot kazasında kaybolan kişiler hakkında neler biliyoruz?

author: Unknown
title: Daxuyaniyên 1ê Îlonê: “Em di aştî û demokratîkbûnê de bi israr in”
content:
Îro 1ê Îlonê Roja Aştiyê ya Cîhanê ye. Li gelek bajaran daxuyanî hate dayîn.


Komeleya Mafên Mirovan (ÎHD) a şaxa Îzmîrê, Şaxa Îzmîrê ya ÎHDê, Platforma Parastin û Hevgirtina Bajarê Amedê,  Rêxistina Navçeya Qovanciyana Xarpêtê Partiya Wekhevî û Demokrasiyê ya Gelan (DEM Partiyê) û Rêxistina DEM Partiyê ya Konyayê têkildarî roja aştiyê daxuyanî dan.


Ji sala 1993yan û heta niha “Hewldanên Aştiyê”


1 Îlon 2023


“Bêdengbûna çekan bi tenê aştiyê nayne”


Destpêkê hevserokê giştî ya ÎHDê Cîhan Aydin axivî û wiha got:


 “Li Tirkiyeyê di çapemeniyê de, bi taybetî jî di çapemeniya ku li dijî aştiyê ye de, atmosfereke ku dixwazin vê veguherînin dijminatiya aştiyê heye. Em vê yekê bi xemgînî dişopînin. Di encamê de, bêdengbûna çekan bi tenê aştiyê nayne. Şer rawestiya lê belê hafizeya vî şerî li cihê xwe disekine. Lewma divê em, yanî ev civak û hemû komên etnîkî û komên baweriyê yên ku di nav vê civakê de wekî dijmin tê dîtin,rastiya ku vî şerî çêkiriye re rû bi rû bimînin. Divê mirov ji miriyan netirse. Divê mirov rêzê li wan bigire. Divê em êşên hatine jiyîn, hemû êşan bêyî ku bi hev re bidin pêşbirkkirin, wekî giştî deynin ser maseya aştî û rastiyê. Em tenê bi vî rengî dikarin aştiya mayînde ava bikin.”


“Çareserî bi pêkanîna mafên mirovan pêkan e”


Piştre endama rêveberiya ÎHDê Nazli Turan jî diyar kir ku aştî bi avakirina sîstemeke civakî ya demokratîk pêkan e lewma aştî mafekî mirovî ye û destnîşan kir ku dîroka nêz a Tirkiyeyê nîşan daye ku pirsgirêka Kurd bi polîtîkayên ewlehîparêz û înkarker nayê çareserkirin û ev tişt anî ziman: 


“Polîtîkayên ewlehîparêz bûne sedema mirina bi hezaran mirovan, koçberkirinê, valakirina gundan, windakirinên bi zorê û kuştinan, îşkence û muameleya xirab û astengkirina gelek maf û azadiyên bingehîn. Weke parêzvanên mafên mirovan wekî ku me bi salan gotiye, çareseriya Pirsgirêka Kurd; ne bi tundî û polîtîkayên ewlehiyê re; bi demokrasi, qanûn, hevwelatîbûna wekhev û xistina meriyetê ya mafên mirovan a bi awayekî giştî re pêkan e. Di qonaxa ku îro hatiye de em dibînin ku pencereyeke nû ya çareseriya aştiyane û demokratîk hatiye vekirin. Lê belê bêdengbûna çekan bi tenê nayê wateya aştiyê. Ji bo ku aştiya mayînde bê dabînkirin, divê gavên qanûnî û destûrî yên pêwîst ji bo çareserkirina pirsgirêkên siyasî, qanûnî û civakî yên ku şer çêdikin, di heman demê de bên avêtin.”


“Şert û mercên Abdullah Ocalan divê ji nû ve bên sazkirin”


Nazli Tûran bal kişand ser şert û mercên Rêberê Gelê Kurd Abdullah Ocalan û got ku Abdullah Ocalan aktorekî girîng ê pêvajoyê ye ji ber vê şert û mercên wî divê ji nû ve bên sererastkirin û wiha pêde çû:


 “Divê bi pêşbînîkirina tecrîda malê yan jî şert û mercên înfazê yên bi vî rengî derfetên hevdîtinê yên bi cîhana derve re bên dabînkirin û ev babet bên girêdan bi mîsyongireke qanûnî. author: anred
title: “Fuera el barco inglés”: repudian el amarre del petrolero VS PROMISE en Ushuaia
content:
El buque VS Promise en el puerto de Ushuaia. Foto: Gentileza Gobierno de Tierra del Fuego.


Izquierda Socialista de Ushuaia y el Frente de Izquierda-Unidad repudiaron el ingreso y amarre del buque petrolero VS PROMISE en el Puerto de Ushuaia y reclamaron explicaciones al Estado nacional y al Gobierno de Tierra del Fuego. La embarcación está registrada en la Isla de Man, dependencia de la Corona británica, y llegó al puerto fueguino (cuya administración se encuentra intervenida por el Gobierno nacional desde enero) luego de haber operado en la terminal petrolera de Río Cullen. El Gobierno provincial repudió la operación y exigió a Nación que informe bajo qué criterios fue autorizada. «Esto no es un tema menor. Tierra del Fuego y el Atlántico Sur no son una ‘zona neutral’: tienen un valor geopolítico estratégico para controlar la entrada a la Antártida, el pasaje bioceánico y las Islas del Atlántico Sur, incluyendo nuestras Islas Malvinas, que se encuentran bajo ocupación colonial británica», señalan. Mientras el VS PROMISE ya dejó Ushuaia y continuó su recorrido, la controversia dejó instalada una discusión que excede a un barco: qué concepción de soberanía existe sobre los puertos, los recursos naturales y el Atlántico Sur, y quién decide sobre ellos.

Por ANRed.


Izquierda Socialista de Ushuaia

 y el

Frente de Izquierda-Unidad

 repudiaron el

ingreso y amarre del buque petrolero VS PROMISE en el Puerto de Ushuaia

 y reclamaron explicaciones al Estado nacional y al Gobierno de Tierra del Fuego. La embarcación, identificada como de bandera británica y registrada en la

Isla de Man

, llegó a Ushuaia el 24 de agosto, en un

puerto cuya administración se encuentra intervenida por el Gobierno nacional desde enero

.


“Esto no es un tema menor.

Tierra del Fuego y el Atlántico Sur no son una ‘zona neutral’: tienen un valor geopolítico estratégico para controlar la entrada a la Antártida, el pasaje bioceánico y las Islas del Atlántico Sur, incluyendo nuestras Islas Malvinas

, que se encuentran bajo ocupación colonial británica”, señalaron desde Izquierda Socialista, que exigió conocer “qué operación realizó, qué transportó y quién autorizó”.


La controversia se profundizó porque el VS PROMISE no llegó directamente desde el exterior: antes había operado en la terminal petrolera de

Río Cullen

, en el norte de Tierra del Fuego. Según un documento de la Dirección Provincial de Puertos difundido por

Agenda Malvinas

 y recogido por medios especializados, el organismo registró su ingreso el 12 de agosto, su partida el 13 y la carga de

22.464,570 toneladas métricas de petróleo crudo

, además de liquidar las tasas correspondientes por la operación.


El buque VS Promise en el puerto de Ushuaia. Foto: Gentileza Gobierno de Tierra del Fuego.


La información contradice la idea de que la operatoria petrolera del buque era desconocida para las autoridades provinciales. El Gobierno de Tierra del Fuego, en tanto, concentró su cuestionamiento en Nación y sostuvo que el buque ingresó al Puerto de Ushuaia mientras la terminal se encuentra “sustraída de la administración provincial” por la intervención de la Agencia Nacional de Puertos y Navegación. En esa línea, la Provincia reclamó que se informe “bajo qué criterios políticos, estratégicos y administrativos se autorizó la operación”.


El trasfondo es además la política hidrocarburífera de la provincia: Río Cullen forma parte de las áreas cuya producción busca garantizar el Gobierno fueguino mientras avanza una nueva licitación luego del vencimiento de la concesión que estaba en manos de una UTE integrada por Roch, Secra, Crownpoint Energía y DPG. En ese escenario, desde Izquierda Socialista apuntaron contra la presencia de empresas que, según denunciaron, tienen antecedentes vinculados con la cuestión Malvinas, y plantearon: “frente a esa realidad, la pregunta vuelve a ser la misma:

¿quién controla? ¿quién audita? ¿quién rinde cuentas? Porque el puerto y el territorio no pueden funcionar como una zona liberada de responsabilidades

”.


La disputa también involucra el control del Puerto de Ushuaia: en enero, la Agencia Nacional de Puertos y Navegación dispuso la suspensión de su habilitación por doce meses, prorrogables, y ordenó su intervención administrativa, argumentando deficiencias operativas y de infraestructura. La norma destacó, al mismo tiempo, el carácter estratégico del puerto por su ubicación en el Atlántico Sur y su cercanía con la Antártida.
